signature.name: Taipei 101
signature.detail: Taipei's defining skyscraper and a symbol of the city, with an observation deck offering sweeping views. Go on a clear day; tickets can be bought on the spot or online, and the best time is late afternoon to catch sunset and city lights.

signature.name: National Palace Museum
signature.detail: Houses one of the world's largest collections of Chinese imperial artifacts, making it a must for history and art lovers. Visit on a weekday morning to avoid crowds; the museum is easily reached by bus or taxi from downtown.

signature.name: Chiang Kai-shek Memorial Hall
signature.detail: A monumental landmark set in a large park, featuring the memorial hall, Liberty Square Arch, and the National Theater. The changing of the guard ceremony is a highlight; go early morning or late afternoon for cooler weather and fewer crowds.

signature.name: Shilin Night Market
signature.detail: Taipei's most famous night market, offering a dizzying array of street food and local snacks. Come hungry and try classics like oyster omelets and giant fried chicken; it's busiest after 7 pm, so arrive earlier for a more comfortable experience.

signature.name: Longshan Temple
signature.detail: A beautifully ornate Buddhist temple that remains an active place of worship, giving visitors a glimpse into local religious life. Dress respectfully and visit in the evening when the temple is beautifully lit and less crowded.

signature.name: Ximending
signature.detail: A vibrant pedestrian shopping and entertainment district, often called Taipei's Harajuku. It's perfect for people-watching, street performances, and trendy shops; go in the evening when the area comes alive with neon lights.

signature.name: Dihua Street
signature.detail: A historic street lined with traditional shops selling Chinese herbs, dried goods, and fabrics, especially lively during Lunar New Year. Wander the side alleys to discover old architecture and sample local snacks; it's a short walk from the MRT.

signature.name: Yehliu Geopark
signature.detail: A unique coastal geological park famous for its mushroom-shaped rock formations, including the iconic Queen's Head. Bring sunscreen and water as there's little shade; it's about an hour's bus ride from Taipei, so plan for a half-day trip.

signature.name: Jiufen Old Street
signature.detail: A charming hillside old street with teahouses, snack stalls, and stunning ocean views, often compared to Spirited Away. Visit on a weekday to avoid crowds, and stay for sunset when the lanterns light up the narrow alleys.
